audit.why: 50% over 20 games. Chart gives Zac levels 3, 4-5 and both item stages with Akshan on 1 and 6, and the mirror at audits/top/zac__akshan.json frames the same lane as 'uphill early, Zac's on scaling'. Consistent from both sides.

Lvl 2-3 poke, Zac's Lvl 6 all-in, the Youmuu's-into-Serpent's-Fang window, and Zac's two-item frontline scaling. Four spikes, correctly owned, and the mirror's spikes agree on the same turning points.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Stretching Strikes a 'short-range Q grab' twice and tells the reader not to 'stand inside his Q grab range' as though that were a comfortable margin. It is 800 range against Akshan's 850 Avengerang. It also never states the condition on the throw: the grab alone does nothing until Zac attacks a SECOND enemy, which is what throws the two together.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Zac stretches an arm, grabbing an enemy. Attacking a different enemy will cause him to throw both targets towards each other', range 800, 14/12.5/11/9.5/8s. An isolated Akshan caught by Q eats a grab and nothing else — knowing that changes whether you panic. And 800 versus 850 means poking at 'max range' leaves fifty units of margin, not a safe buffer. The mirror states the two-target requirement from Zac's side ('the knock-together needs two'), so both directions now agree.
audit.corrected: Stretching Strikes is 800 range, 14s at rank 1, and the throw requires him to hit a second target. Unstable Matter (W, 350, 5s) is the genuinely short-range ability.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'When his E sling is on cooldown' is the entry's central instruction and appears four times with no number.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 — an enormous window against a ranged champion, and the difference between 'wait a beat' and 'take the whole wave'. The mirror uses the same figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things the reader needs and the page never says: Cell Division's revive is on a flat 5 MINUTE cooldown, and Unstable Matter deals a percentage of MAX health.
audit.why: Riot's text for Cell Division: 'Upon taking fatal damage, Zac splits into 4 bloblets... This ability has a 5 minute cooldown.' The entry calls him 'unkillable' — he is not; a Zac who has already used it is a normal health bar, and that is the window to force objectives. Riot's text for Unstable Matter: 'dealing a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', so building durability against him is the wrong instinct. The mirror surfaced the 5-minute figure from Zac's side.

edits.after: Trade off terrain with E, but respect Stretching Strikes at 800 — only Unstable Matter (W) is truly short

edits.before: Zac is a tank you can actually poke — he's melee, short-range, and his only gap-close is a telegraphed E sling, so farm with Q out-and-back and chip him on every step-up. The catch is his passive: every ability drops blobs he walks over to heal, so a single poke doesn't stick — you have to land your Q return hit plus the passive second shot faster than he reassembles. Don't stand inside his Q grab range while you chase a poke, and back off the instant you see him charging E at you.
edits.after: Zac is a tank you can actually poke — he's melee, and his only gap-close is a telegraphed Elastic Slingshot (E) on 21s, so farm with Q out-and-back and chip him on every step-up. Two catches. Cell Division sheds blobs he walks over to heal, so stomp them or land the Q return hit plus the second shot faster than he reassembles. And Stretching Strikes reaches 800 against your 850 — 'outside grab range' is fifty units of margin, not a safe buffer.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your window — E Heroic Swing fires while you swing around terrain, so you can trade from angles his short kit can't punish and bleed him faster than the blobs heal. But at 6 the math shifts: a charged E sling onto your squishy, shieldless body lets his Q grab and W slam land for a full combo, and your R is a ranged execute, not a brawling button to answer it point-blank. Keep E off cooldown as your escape, and only commit a real all-in when his E sling is on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your window — Heroic Swing fires while you arc around terrain and it dodges a telegraphed Elastic Slingshot outright, so bait the 21s sling and bleed him faster than the blobs heal. At 6 the math shifts: a landed sling lets Stretching Strikes and Unstable Matter connect on your shieldless body, and your R is a ranged execute, not a brawling button to answer it point-blank. Keep E as your escape and commit only once the sling is spent.

edits.before: This evens out and then tips his way — a two-item Zac is a rubber-ball with thousands of HP, and your lethality burst stops mattering once he can eat your full R and blob it back. He becomes a frontline that E-slings onto your carries and peels you off with grab and slam. Win your tempo on the first-item spike and take the lane to the map — roam with camo W for picks, because if the game goes long, his durability beats your damage.
edits.after: This evens out and then tips his way — a two-item Zac is a rubber-ball with thousands of HP, and Unstable Matter bills you a share of your MAX health, so durability is the wrong answer. But he is not unkillable: Cell Division's revive is a flat 5 MINUTE cooldown, so a Zac who already used it is one ordinary health bar and that is your objective window. Win tempo on the first-item spike and roam with camo W for picks.

edits.after: Heroic Swing fires while you arc around terrain and dodges the Elastic Slingshot outright — bait the 21s sling, then swing in.

edits.before: Two-item Zac out-grows your lethality: thousands of HP eat your full R and he peels your team with E sling and grab.
edits.after: Two-item Zac out-grows your lethality, and Unstable Matter bills a share of your MAX health every 5s regardless of armour.

notes: Reused the mirror at audits/top/zac__akshan.json rather than re-deriving: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1, Heroic Swing dodging it, the Stretching Strikes throw requiring a second target, and Cell Division's 5-minute revive cooldown. All four now read the same from both sides. The two corrections that matter most on Akshan's page are the ones the mirror could not make for him: Stretching Strikes was called 'short-range' twice when it is 800 against his own 850, so the entry was selling a safety margin that barely exists; and 'unkillable' was doing a lot of work for an ability with a flat five-minute cooldown, which is a concrete objective window rather than a permanent condition. Also added that Unstable Matter is percent-MAX-health, which is why building durability into him is the wrong instinct.
unverified: The kit file tags Elastic Slingshot with a 'grounding' flag ('shuts off enemy dashes'). Riot's own description — 'Zac attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward' — contains no grounding effect, so I treated the flag as a tooltip-parsing misfire and wrote nothing about it. If Zac genuinely grounds, it would matter enormously here, since grounding would disable Heroic Swing; worth one wiki check before anyone acts on the flag either way.
